title: Velocity-Time Graphs
short: On a v–t graph the slope is the acceleration and the area under the line is the displacement.
trouble: Students read a v–t graph as if it showed position, thinking a downward slope means moving backward.

blocks.html: A velocity-time ($v$–$t$) graph looks like the x–t graphs you know, but it answers different questions. Its height is the velocity, and two features carry the rest of the story: its slope and the area under it.
On a $v$–$t$ graph, the slope is the Acceleration and Its Sign and the area between the graph and the time axis is the displacement (area below the axis counts as negative).

Slope: rise over run is $\Delta v / \Delta t$, which is the definition of acceleration. Area: at a steady velocity, displacement is $v \times \Delta t$, which is the area of a rectangle of height $v$ and width $\Delta t$. When $v$ changes, slice the time into thin strips; each strip is nearly a rectangle, so adding the strips adds up the little displacements. Shapes from Area of a Trapezoid do the adding for you when the pieces are straight.

blocks.name: ph-motion

opts.task: Drag the corners of the v–t graph to design a motion. Make part of it negative and watch the cart back up and the area turn red.

blocks.cap: Design a motion on the v–t graph. The shaded area always equals the cart's displacement.

blocks.title: Slope gives acceleration
blocks.q: A cart's velocity rises in a straight line from $2\ \text{m/s}$ at $t = 0$ to $8\ \text{m/s}$ at $t = 3\ \text{s}$. Find its acceleration.

blocks.title: Area gives displacement
blocks.q: For that same cart (from $2$ to $8\ \text{m/s}$ in $3\ \text{s}$), how far does it go?
steps: The area under the line is a trapezoid with parallel sides $2$ and $8\ \text{m/s}$ and width $3\ \text{s}$.

blocks.title: Area below the axis
blocks.q: A cart moves at $+4\ \text{m/s}$ for $3\ \text{s}$, then at $-2\ \text{m/s}$ for $2\ \text{s}$. Find its displacement and the distance it travels.
steps: Area above the axis: $4 \times 3 = 12\ \text{m}$. Area below: $-2 \times 2 = -4\ \text{m}$.

blocks.html: Reading a $v$–$t$ graph as if it showed position, so a downward slope "means moving backward". A downward slope means the velocity is decreasing; the cart still moves forward as long as the graph is above the axis. Check: direction of motion comes from the sign of $v$ (above or below the axis); the slope only says whether $v$ is going up or down.
